name: Heliodorus
bio: Heliodorus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no firm date for the poet. Paton's index describes him as the author of the Aethiopica.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 485, 490).

poems.title: Book IX, 485: From his Aethiopica, iii. 2
poems.author: Heliodorus
poems.text: I sina Thetis, golden-haired Thetis, the immortal daughter of the sea-god Nereus, who by the counsel of Zeus wedded Peleus, the glory of the sea, our Aphrodite, her who bore from her womb the raging spearman, the Ares of war, the lightning of Greece, divine Achilles, whose glory reaches to heaven. By him Pyrrha bore Neoptolemus, the sacker of Troy and saviour of Greece. Be gracious unto us, blessed hero Neoptolemus, now lying in Delphian earth ; receive favourably this sacrifice and ward off all fear from our city. Thetis I sing, golden-haired Thetis.

poems.title: Book IX, 490: From his Aethiopica, viii. 11
poems.author: Heliodorus
poems.text: When wearing the stone Pantarbes (Fear-all), fear not the force of fire. The unexpected is easy for the Fates.
